title: Mock 1
description: Core conversions, Boolean logic and ARM fundamentals.

questions.title: Architecture and coding
questions.prompt: Select one answer in each part.

parts.label: In a Von Neumann architecture, instructions and data…
A Unicode code point identifies…
parts.answer: a character independently of its UTF encoding
options: a character independently of its UTF encoding
exactly one byte in every UTF encoding

questions.why: Von Neumann uses shared instruction/data memory. A code point is an abstract character identifier; an encoding determines how it is stored.

questions.title: Unsigned conversions
questions.prompt: Use unsigned values. Follow each answer format exactly.

parts.label: Convert decimal 173 to exactly 8 binary digits.
Convert binary 11010110 to hexadecimal, without a prefix or leading zeros.

questions.title: Two’s complement
questions.prompt: All bit patterns in this question are 8-bit two’s complement.

parts.label: Encode decimal −37 as exactly 8 binary digits.
Encode decimal −37 as exactly 2 hex digits, with no prefix.
Decode 11101010 to a signed decimal integer.

questions.why: 37 = 00100101; invert and add 1 to get 11011011 = DB. For 11101010, unsigned 234 − 256 = −22.

questions.title: Unsigned binary fractions
questions.prompt: Convert decimal 6.6875 to unsigned binary. Use no prefix, no leading zeros and exactly 4 digits after the binary point.

questions.title: Encode IEEE 754
questions.prompt: Encode decimal −13.25 as IEEE 754 single precision (binary32).

parts.label: Complete representation: 0x followed by exactly 8 hex digits

questions.title: Boolean laws
questions.prompt: Choose the valid identity in each part. A prime (') means NOT; + means OR; juxtaposition means AND.
questions.why: De Morgan exchanges AND/OR and complements the operands. Absorption: A+AB=A. A OR NOT A is always 1.

questions.title: Three-variable Karnaugh map
questions.prompt:
Simplify the map to a minimal sum of products. Columns BC are in Gray-code order. Group 1s, including wrapping groups.
Output F
A \ BC00011110
01001
11111
Use ASCII primes, no spaces, no AND dots, and alphabetical variable order within terms.
questions.why: The entire A=1 row gives A. The first and last columns wrap to make a four-cell group with C=0, giving C'. Thus F=A+C'.

questions.title: Four-variable Karnaugh map
questions.prompt:
Simplify to a minimal sum of products. Both axes use Gray-code order.
Output F
AB \ CD00011110
001100
010000
110011
101111
Use ASCII primes, no spaces or AND dots, and alphabetical variable order within terms.
questions.why: Rows 00 and 10 wrap: their columns 00 and 01 form a four-cell group B'C'. Rows 11 and 10 in columns 11 and 10 form a four-cell group AC. Together AC+B'C' covers all 1s.

questions.title: ARM fundamentals
questions.prompt: Assume ARMv7 A32 with 32-bit registers throughout this section.

parts.label: Which instruction updates condition flags without storing its subtraction result?
What does ldr r0, =arr obtain?
options: the first byte stored at arr

questions.why: cmp sets flags as if subtracting its second operand from its first. ldr r0, =arr is a pseudo-instruction that obtains an address, whereas ldr r0, [r1] loads memory contents.

questions.title: Byte ordering
questions.prompt: A byte-addressable memory stores the THREE-BYTE value 0xA1B2C3 starting at 0x0020. Fill each blank from the byte options. Drag a chip onto a select box or choose with the keyboard.
questions.why: Little endian stores C3 B2 A1 at ascending addresses 0020–0022. Big endian stores A1 B2 C3. Bits inside each byte keep their order. Options may be reused across the independent cases.

questions.title: Bitwise instruction trace
questions.prompt:
mov r0, #0x3c
mov r1, #0xa5
eor r2, r0, r1
and r3, r0, r1
orr r4, r0, r1
Enter each result as 0x followed by exactly 8 hexadecimal digits.
questions.why: 3C = 00111100 and A5 = 10100101. XOR gives 99, AND gives 24 and OR gives BD. The upper 24 bits remain zero.

questions.title: Single-line C to ARM
questions.prompt: Variables are mapped to the registers with the same names. Write one lowercase ARM instruction per part, using explicit three-operand arithmetic.
questions.why: ARM destination comes first. # marks an immediate constant. lsl shifts left; for unsigned values the stored result is the low 32 bits.

questions.title: Complete an if–else
questions.prompt:
Complete the assembly so it matches the signed C code. Each option may be used once; unused options are distractors. 
if (r2 < r3)
    r0 = r2 + r3;
else
    r0 = r2 - r3;
cmp r2, r3
bge else_case
[blank 1]
[blank 2]
else_case:
[blank 3]
end_if:
questions.why: bge takes the false case when signed r2≥r3. The true case adds, then b end_if skips the else body. The else case subtracts r3 from r2.

questions.title: Trace and identify a program
questions.prompt:
Treat r1 and r2 as signed 32-bit integers. Execution ends at done. 
cmp r1, r2
ble select_r1
mov r0, r2
b done
select_r1:
mov r0, r1
done:

parts.label: r0 when r1=−3 and r2=2 (signed decimal)

questions.why: ble selects r1 when r1≤r2; otherwise r2 is selected. It computes the signed minimum, including for negative inputs.

questions.title: Word and byte loads
questions.prompt:
Assume little endian; each .word is four bytes. Enter 0x followed by exactly 8 hex digits. 
.data
.balign 4
arr: .word 0x10203040, 0x55667788, 0xAABBCCDD
.text
ldr r0, =arr
mov r1, #1
ldrb r2, [r0, r1, lsl #2]
ldr r3, [r0, #8]
questions.why: The scaled index is 1×4=4, selecting the second word. ldrb reads its lowest-address byte 88 and zero-extends it. Offset 8 selects the entire third word for ldr.

questions.title: Match C and assembly
questions.prompt:
Select the signed C block equivalent to this assembly. No overflow occurs. 
mov r0, #0
mov r1, #1
loop:
cmp r1, #5
bge done
add r0, r0, r1
add r1, r1, #1
b loop
done:
questions.why: The comparison precedes the body, and bge exits at r1=5. The added values are 1,2,3,4; final r0=10 and r1=5.

questions.title: Complete repeated-subtraction division
questions.prompt:
For nonnegative inputs here, this program produces quotient r0 and remainder r1. Execution ends at exit. Use one lowercase instruction for the blank, then give decimal results. 
mov r2, #53
mov r3, #7
mov r0, #0
mov r1, #0
[missing instruction]
while_test:
cmp r1, r3
blt exit
sub r1, r1, r3
add r0, r0, #1
b while_test
exit:
questions.why: Initialise the remainder candidate to the dividend using mov r1, r2. Seven subtractions remove 49 from 53, leaving 4. An eighth subtraction is prevented by blt. Thus 53=7×7+4.
